entities.name: Muslim conquest of Persia
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Muslim conquest of Persia, also known as the Arab conquest of Persia, took place in the 7th century CE and lasted from 633 to 654 CE. 

This pivotal event saw the Sasanian Empire, which had ruled Persia for over 400 years, collapse under the onslaught of Arab forces. The conquest led to the spread of Islam in the region and had a profound impact on the politics, culture, and society of Persia.

The Muslim conquest of Persia was a complex and multifaceted process, with various Arab tribes and leaders playing key roles. The conquest culminated in the establishment of an Arab governorate in Persia, which would eventually become a major center of Islamic learning and culture.

One of the most lasting legacies of the Muslim conquest of Persia is the spread of Islam in the region. By the 8th century CE, Persia had become a major hub of Islamic learning and culture, with scholars such as Al-Khwarizmi and Al-Ghazali making significant contributions to the development of Islamic thought.

In the words of the Arab historian Al-Tabari, 'The conquest of Persia was a turning point in the history of Islam, marking the beginning of a new era of expansion and growth for the Muslim world.'
